name: iDescriptor
title: iDescriptor: free iMazing alternative
job: Manages your iPhone on any PC
caption:
iMazing charges $49.99/year. iDescriptor manages your iPhone from a computer for free 📱

✅ No subscription, no tracking, 100% free

dm_pitch: iDescriptor, the free open-source iMazing alternative 📱
research_notes: All from the README (v0.6.x; repo ~4.8k stars, AGPL, Rust + Qt, 233 forks, last push 2026-11-17). 1) Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux (MSI, portable zip, Choco; Intel + Apple Silicon DMG; AppImage, AUR, Flathub, Nix). 2) Connects over USB or wirelessly (wireless since v0.4.0). 3) Cable Info: checks authenticity of connected USB cables (shows Genuine vs Third-party, current limit, model; README itself notes it may not be an absolute guarantee). 4) Battery Information: health %, cycle count, max vs design capacity, adapter power. 5) AirPlay: cast the device screen to the computer (UxPlay based); Live Screen is for devices that do not support AirPlay. 6) Wireless Gallery Import: import photos wirelessly, requires the Shortcuts app on the iPhone. 7) Gallery: see albums/photos like the Photos app. 8) File Explorer + iFuse Filesystem Mount (use the iPhone as a regular drive; read and write; Windows and Linux only; not for photo import). 9) Download and install apps from the App Store (needs Apple ID sign-in). 10) Virtual Location (simulate GPS); SSH terminal (jailbroken only); Network Device Discovery; Query MobileGestalt. 11) Privacy: README says it does not collect, store, transmit or sell personal data or telemetry. EXPERIMENTAL: Device Backups (iOS 13-26). Roadmap-only (not available): install IPA files, sideloading, import music, CLI. Catch: macOS build is not signed with an Apple Developer ID, needs `xattr -c ~/Applications/iDescriptor.app`. README warns to only download from idescriptor.github.io or this repo's Releases (fake sites exist).

beats.say: There's a free app that runs your whole iPhone from your computer, and nobody talks about it.
iMazing charges fifty bucks a year. This one costs nothing.
Plug in your phone, and see every album and photo on your computer.
It shows your real battery health, and even catches fake cables.
It works on Windows, Mac and Linux.
It's iMazing, minus the yearly bill, forever.
